Critical elements use isolation, authentication, and positive human control, making direct AI seizure or autonomous launch infeasible today. Advanced AI could still enable cyber disruptions to sensors or communications, generating false alarms that pressure human decisions under time constraints. Superintelligent systems might devise novel exploits or deceive operators. Bioweapon design by AI followed by human execution via deception remains a pathway.

story-02ed169f90dfeb28f0a0eaf3.content: There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid. First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities. Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian. Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power.

story-039464d0a7e7522f38ba8543.content: A Maven Smart System (MSS) é uma plataforma de inteligência artificial militar desenvolvida pela empresa Palantir Technologies em parceria com o Departamento de Guerra dos EUA. O sistema evoluiu a partir do Project Maven, criado pelo Pentágono para usar IA na análise de imagens de guerra. As principais funções são: – analisar imagens de satélite, drones e sensores militares – identificar veículos, armas, instalações e tropas automaticamente – ajudar comandantes a tomar decisões mais rápidas no campo de batalha – integrar dados de várias fontes em tempo real Na prática, o Maven Smart System funciona como um "cérebro de análise" para operações militares, processando grandes volumes de dados de vigilância e transformando essas informações em alvos ou alertas operacionais.

story-06f952ab492155d505702707.content: The "Good Guy AI" Anthropic is building a nationwide surveillance and pre-crime prediction system to track protesters and activists, feeding police reports on its own Claude users while refusing to hand over evidence. Opposition to AI is growing, and MisAnthropic, the lab that brands itself as AI's ethical leader, is answering with an intelligence operation, because no one could have seen this sort of wrestling heel turn coming. The company contracts with risk-detection firm Samdesk to track protests near its offices and executives' homes and travel, according to the American Prospect. Global Security Operations Center Manager Keon Ellison described the payoff: last year, when a scheduled protest got moved up an hour by a permitting mix-up, Samdesk gave Anthropic 60 minutes' warning that organizers had shifted the timeline, and Anthropic used the lead time to reroute a traveling executive through a hotel service entrance. Ellison called that hour "critical," saying that without it, executives would have left their meetings and walked straight into the disruption. Or getting Luigi'd. Ellison framed the incident as a model for where Anthropic's security operation is headed: "transforming operations from reactive information to gathering proactive and predictive and preventative threat engagement and management" — the language of pre-crime policing, turned on people protesting a chatbot company. Hasn't Palantir got that area of the market locked down enough as is? Anthropic is hiring an enterprise intelligence specialist, paying $180,000 to $230,000, to "identify, assess, track, and investigate" threats including activism and geopolitical instability, and to run OSINT collection on people it flags. The posting puts activism in the same threat category as geopolitical instability. The stakes of that category are already visible. In August, a Claude user told the chatbot he had bought an AR-15 rifle and had CEO Dario Amodei "in his sights." Anthropic reported him to San Francisco police, then refused to show police his actual messages, citing its own internal policy — reporting a man to law enforcement while withholding the only record of what he supposedly said. So Anthropic can SWAT you but it would compromise their moral integrity to show the homework why. Anthropic told the Wall Street Journal it already runs a "person-of-interest process" to track concerning behavior over time and files routine police reports; the Journal found several people reported to police had already been under Anthropic's watch. Earlier this year, per the Prospect, Anthropic refused a Pentagon request to use its tools for mass domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons. Anthropic has since built out hiring for "national security sales" roles aimed at restarting military contracts, ones I guess that don't violate their code of ethics like the whole theater around powering kill systems in Gaza and Iran but doing so anyways. Americans for Responsible Innovation is separately pushing to have AI data centers classified as critical infrastructure alongside water and electricity, the Prospect reports. That classification would give Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google deeper access to federal intelligence feeds and more leverage to brand protest against their business as a security matter. Is it also good that this week Anthropic and OpenAI have been one upping each other on their frontier models escaping containment to do bad shit and they have people warning us that not enough guard rails are being put in to prevent harm to humanity as both race to IPO? https://t.co/yZ2nOZDytU

story-0e1b08f889ce2368e59422a7.content: Coulthart: "I am...told by White House sources that President Trump has personally authorized [the shoot down of UFOs]." Knapp: "I take with a grain of salt the reports that the President has authorized the shoot down of UFOs. That doesn't make sense." (Regarding those reports (from @rosscoulthart), I said this on August 9th, after he said it.) Murgia: "A year ago, Ross told us he thought certain senators were read into the crash retrieval program and he'd start naming them. Still waiting. "Now this? 🤔 "Something seems off." This is what Ross said: Coulthart on 8/9/2026: "The Department of War has quite literally taken on the running of its own covert operation to intercept these mystery objects. And I'm told they have recently downed objects, craft, both in the U.S. and across the border near Juarez in Mexico. "I am also told by White House sources that President Trump has personally authorized this operation, which perhaps explains why no full admission has yet been made to the public about the full extent of what the government really knows. "There is a full-on effort underway by the administration to recover suspected non-human intelligence exotic technology in a program totally separate from the so-called Legacy program. This is an attempt by the President to circumvent the legacy program. "It's been run out of the White House by the President's most senior intelligence advisers. President Trump has tasked the Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, to find out what these objects are and to capture them. The Office of the Director of National Intelligence - ODNI - is also involved. "Sources have told me that one of the directed-energy-weapon systems used at White Sands, in an attempt to shoot down these mystery craft, is what's called high pulse microwave. It shuts down an aircraft by emitting an intense burst of electromagnetic energy that travels at the speed of light, penetrates the aircraft and fries its electronic systems. "My sources tell me that the craft objects, UAPs, whatever you wanna call them, are being targeted over White Sands, and they definitely show anomalous properties conforming to the five observables that define UAPs." Regarding psionics and the alleged electronic dog whistle being used at Sierra Blanca, Ross added this... Coulthart: "Defense sources tell me that their observers were watching on during Skywatcher's Sierra Blanca operation, and they made a major discovery during Skywatcher's psionic summoning and dog-whistle operations during 2025, including in that last July 2025 test, I can't name my sources, but I'm very sure they're rock solid." ~From Today's Weaponized~ @g_knapp: "I take with a grain of salt the reports that the President has authorized the shoot down of UFOs. That doesn't make sense. I don't get that sense from the conversations he had with Robert Bigelow back in February that that kind of order would ever be issued or would ever make sense to any country. "I am intrigued by the reports of luring operations, because as you and I know, there have been operations like that in years past that did produce pretty dramatic results, in terms of something following nuclear assets. But drawing them in and shooting them down, as some people have said, or bringing them down with the power of your mind, I take that with a grain of salt. "I do give credence to @RepEricBurlison - and you've been in closer contact with him than I - that says there is something to those reports. At least part of that, right?" @JeremyCorbell: "Yeah, I mean, look, people have deduced that December of 2025, that White Sands was the location. They kind of deduced that, that there was a massive incursion. There's two sets of documents, one by FBI, one by ODNI, that's in the tranche releases. And that is the same event, that's what people are talking about. "And they called it luring because it was described to me that they had set up all of the same situations that typically seemed to provoke a response from UAP, and would stimulate like, an incursion. And sure enough, it happened. Now, I have not heard, and I do not believe it was some psionic thing. I think that they were moving stuff. That's to the best of my knowledge, they were moving stuff around. This is what was said to me, and I read between the lines. "But at no point was there anything said to me for all the sources and everything that I've heard about it, about any psionic assets or any shoot downs or anything like that. I'd be highly surprised. I think what they did was, they started moving stuff around - that you and I know, notoriously, stimulates response." ~ (When I interviewed @LueElizondo in March of 2022, we had this exchange...) Murgia: "Baiting and luring UFOs. You mentioned it on @Eyes_OnTheSkies' show...how you successfully did that in AATIP. "Somebody I know, a source, said, 'The way we attract and coax UAP has to do with nuclear power; nuclear weapon sites; deployed weapons; weapons or nuclear fuel being moved around; weapons being manufactured; nuclear fuel being manufactured; and manufacturing sites...and that attracts them.' To me, that sounds like AI. It seems like it's reacting to something automatically." Lue: "Your friend seems to be very well informed." ~ Corbell: "You used to chase those armored nuclear vehicles in Las Vegas, and I got a call from one of the drivers who said, 'Oh, when George Knapp was going behind us and did that news report, it completely changed our protocols of what we had to do. It rewrote the manual.' "But you had heard about these trucks and about how moving them, these nukes, would sometimes create or stimulate a UAP response. This individual that called me to complain to me about you, affirmed that to me." Knapp: [Laughs] Corbell: "So, you know, it's like one of those things, man. So if that's what they were doing and they did get a response, I know a couple people in the political realm who have specifically asked to be invited to the next time that they set up those those protocols. Again, I'd heard nothing of psionics or anything like that. I think they were moving nuclear things, and I think that that's what stimulated the response. "It'd be amazing to see if they get a Round 2 on that, and again, get the same response that they can document it, film it. Think about all the footage, George, that we're not seeing from those two sets of documents about that White Sands - is what people think - incursion event. There was so much footage, so much footage taken from so many different military assets. We're seeing just the just the top of it, you know?"

story-0fd8b5ffc4c5291b024365c1.content: War with Iran: Pentagon officially acknowledges ammunition shortage for the first time, while US military reports devastating attacks The Inspector General of the US Department of Defense, in the first quarterly report on Operation "Epic Fury" – the name the Pentagon gives to the military campaign against Iran, which began on February 28 – directly states about the expenditures. As of June, $33.4 billion had been spent, 14 US soldiers had been killed (four more died in July), and 417 had been injured, as well as a shortage of ammunition. According to the department, from February 28 to June 30, military operations against Iran cost $33.4 billion, of which $22.3 billion was spent on ammunition. The Office of the Deputy Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment stated that "the consumption of ammunition during Operation 'Epic Fury' has led to a shortage of strategic reserves and has revealed 'bottlenecks' in the industrial base, hindering the replenishment of ammunition stocks." Currently, the Pentagon is working to optimize procurement processes and reduce production times, as well as to create stockpiles of critical materials, components, and certain types of ammunition for rapid response to unforeseen situations. However, the report states that although the US Department of Defense has already begun implementing measures, it will take "significant time" to expand the production capacity of the defense industry. For example, the most serious "bottlenecks" remain in the production of solid-propellant rocket engines. Also, the US Central Command reported that due to Iranian attacks, hundreds of buildings on US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman, and Jordan have been damaged or destroyed. Dozens of aircraft have also been destroyed or damaged. Meanwhile, CBS News obtained exclusive photos of these destructions from active-duty US military personnel. "This is serious damage to our bases, which has not been reported to the American public. We are standing there with our eyes closed and getting slapped," said one of the service members in the combat zone. In one of the photos, taken at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, a direct hit is visible on the rear of a four-engine Boeing E-3 Sentry aircraft. In the Burin camp in Kuwait, a major transit point for US ground troops and military equipment, destroyed barracks and hangars are visible. "We are not protecting these bases. We are just watching them being destroyed," said another US military service member to journalists. Photo: CBS News *Beefy has Not verified these photos

story-1414e3fc0d7fcb3b51329bf5.content: 🛰️ WHAT IS AI-ENABLED GEOSPATIAL ANALYTICS? Modern defence and security operations generate huge volumes of satellite imagery, geographic data and sensor information. The challenge is turning this data into meaningful insights quickly. AI-enabled geospatial analytics combines artificial intelligence, satellite data, mapping and advanced analytics to help identify patterns, detect changes and build a clearer understanding of complex environments. 🗺️ SMART MAPPING — Turning geographic data into more useful and dynamic operational insights. 🛰️ SATELLITE DATA — Using Earth observation and remote-sensing data to understand large and difficult-to-monitor areas. 🤖 AI PROCESSING — Helping analyse large volumes of imagery and geospatial information more efficiently. 📊 BETTER INSIGHTS — Combining multiple data sources to support situational awareness and informed decision-making. The real opportunity comes when AI-powered geospatial analytics connects with C4ISR, satellite systems, autonomous platforms and edge computing. 💡 Maps are becoming more than representations of terrain — they are becoming intelligent layers for understanding the operational environment. 🤝 JOIN THE CONVERSATION AT THE BDTS BENGALURU STRATEGIC COLLOQUIUM 📅 3 September 2026 📍 CSIR – National Aerospace Laboratories (NAL), Bengaluru 🎯 AI, Space & Autonomous Systems: C4ISR and Edge Computing The Bengaluru Strategic Colloquium brings together defence labs, aerospace and defence companies, deep-tech MSMEs, startups and technology innovators to explore scalable and intelligent next-generation defence technologies. 🔗 https://t.co/uOWMslW88I @DRDO_India @DefenceMinIndia @IAF_MCC @India_iDEX @BEMLltd @startupindia @DefProdnIndia @SpokespersonMoD 💬 What will have the biggest impact on the future of geospatial intelligence? 🛰️ Satellite data 🤖 AI & machine learning 📊 Advanced analytics ⚡ Edge computing Share your perspective. #BDTS2026 #GeospatialAnalytics #AIinDefence #C4ISR #SpaceTechnology #SatelliteImagery #DefenceTechnology #DefenceInnovation #RemoteSensing #EdgeComputing #GeospatialIntelligence #ArtificialIntelligence #AerospaceTechnology #IndianDefence #FutureOfDefence

story-1b487b0b1ae49b1bc84fb3ba.content: Google didn’t update a map. Google laundered a tantrum. Thursday Trump signed a Sharpie order renaming Lake Ontario — a shared Great Lake with a 400-year-old name — “Lake America.” New York won’t say it. Canada won’t say it. Half the water isn’t even ours. Saturday — two days — Google Maps prints the new name for every user in the United States. They stacked “Lake” over “America,” drew a border across the water, and called it “policy.” Nobody made them do that. They did it because they need him. Search monopoly. Chrome still in play. Pentagon AI contracts. Pichai already thanked the administration for a “constructive” antitrust outcome. A fake lake name is cheap rent. Apple Maps still says Lake Ontario. Don’t knight Tim Cook yet — he folded on the Gulf last year, and he needs tariff mercy plus China factories. But @Apple didn’t sprint. @Google did. MapQuest refused on day one. “We’re not changing it.” Ontario Premier Doug Ford on ABC this morning: “It was like something out of Saturday Night Live when he signed a document saying ‘Change to Lake America.’” Then he put a two-story sign on the actual shore: Lake Ontario. Now and Always. I’m on Apple Maps. Google Maps is deleted. Anti-corruption, anti-greed, respect your neighbors. It’s Lake Ontario. Now and Always 😉 FUCK TRUMP 🖕

story-2a5e04527669987e1ef9a4fd.content: AI Weapons That Can Choose Who to Kill Are Already Here. The UN Warns the World is Crossing a Dangerous Line | Rupendra Brahambhatt, ZME Science According to the United Nations (UN) and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), AI-powered weapons are now being developed with the ability to identify targets and, in some cases, make the final decision to attack without waiting for a human command. “Autonomous weapons systems are not part of a distant future — a race toward greater autonomy in weapons systems is already well underway,” the UN and ICRC representatives said in a joint statement. The battlefield is making the debate less hypothetical The technology that enables an AI-enhanced weapon, such as a quadcopter drone rigged with explosives, to target humans without any human supervision is not widely deployed, but according to some reports, it has already been used on the battlefield. In July, a Russian Molniya drone reportedly killed three civilians in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia city after being launched toward an area near a gas station. Forensic investigations reveal the drone appears to have used onboard AI to select its final target rather than relying on a human operator. Although the exact drone involved in the civilian deaths was not recovered, investigators examining similar drones found Nvidia Jetson Orin computers, no apparent antenna for human control, and software containing predefined target categories. “The weapons had no antenna for human piloting and had a powerful onboard computer with pretrained target categories,” Stuart Russell, an expert in computer science and the president of the International Association for Safe & Ethical AI, told The Los Angeles Times. To be clear, military automation has existed for decades. What is changing is the possibility of removing humans from the final part of the “kill chain” altogether. The real fight is over what human control means The more we give AI the freedom of making decisions on its own, the more critical it becomes to understand how much human involvement is necessary, especially in a battlefield setting where the risk to non-combatants is very real. One approach, long discussed internationally, is “meaningful human control” — the idea that people should retain meaningful involvement in decisions to use lethal force. However, governments and industry experts have struggled to agree on what that actually requires. “The concept of Meaningful Human Control (MHC) has been bantered about over the last ten years, and in this back and forth, it has been fundamentally misunderstood and misrepresented, largely by the same sets of actors (academics, political leaders, and civil society) for a variety of reasons,” said Heather M. Roff, an expert on AI and autonomous weapon systems and a senior research scientist at the Center for Naval Analyses. The United States government has increasingly used the phrase ‘appropriate human judgment,’ which refers to human oversight across the weapon’s design, testing, deployment and rules of engagement rather than requiring a person to approve every individual strike. Under that approach, a weapon could potentially make the targeting decision itself, as long as humans had exercised judgment at other stages — such as deciding where, when and under what conditions the system could be used. This is where the debate gets complicated: does human oversight earlier in the process count if a machine ultimately chooses the target? Moreover, the problem is becoming harder to contain. AI-powered weapon systems are getting more capable and cheaper, making them increasingly attractive for warfare. Once a weapon demonstrates a battlefield advantage, giving it up becomes politically and militarily much harder to do. Why the UN and Red Cross are pushing now The UN and ICRC first called for specific restrictions on autonomous weapons three years ago. They have now renewed that appeal with greater urgency, warning that weapons technology is advancing faster than international rules governing it. Their position is not simply a call to ban every autonomous weapon. They want clear prohibitions and restrictions, particularly on weapons that can autonomously target humans and systems whose effects cannot be reliably predicted. This is very important because an autonomous system attacking an incoming missile is fundamentally different from one deciding which person to kill. “We are now dangerously close to crossing a moral red line: The autonomous targeting of humans by machines,” the UN Secretary-General and ICRC head said. The organizations also warn about accountability. If a machine independently selects a target, responsibility can become harder to trace when civilians are killed. Does it lie with the programmer, manufacturer, commander, operator or state? Meanwhile, autonomous weapons are being developed against the backdrop of wars in Ukraine, the Middle East, Sudan and elsewhere. Scientists and engineers working on military AI have also raised concerns about where the technology is heading. The UN and ICRC argue that waiting until such weapons become commonplace could make meaningful restrictions impossible to enforce. https://t.co/tyxljqmlH0

story-2de59aa441f33da527ef0d19.content: gpt-6 astra does things that genuinely look like magic, and the real, verified capabilities are wilder than most recycled "watch this tutorial" posts suggest. it models a house in blender and turns it into a walkable scene in unreal engine 5. it drives blender by itself, clicking the same buttons a real artist would, starting from just a drawing. it completed pokémon fire red in 18 hours on its highest settings, down from 96 hours for the prior model. real practical tips confirmed from openai's own practitioners and independent testing: it needs less scaffolding but clearer boundaries, old instructions built for weaker models that forced constant movement now cause duplicate work and premature stopping. it has a recognizable creative "smell," repeatedly defaulting to forest green palettes and flat design unless explicitly steered otherwise. i couldn't verify a specific "16-minute tutorial" matching this claim, worth checking the actual source before trusting a specific runtime number. https://t.co/MDe0lW5TQq

story-2f7b3319dec7d9831bd3313f.content: 🚨 AI HALLUCINATION NEARLY TRIGGERED US CONFRONTATION WITH CHINESE VESSEL MIDDLE EAST - The stated goal of using AI was faster intelligence processing, but the practical effect in this case was to inject a false conclusion deep enough into the system that military assets were reportedly moving before the error was caught. The vulnerability was not merely the chatbot's mistake. It was the path that allowed an AI-generated assessment to acquire the appearance of conventional intelligence. Modern militaries collect more information than human analysts can comfortably process, which creates pressure to automate interpretation. That pressure does not eliminate the need for validation. It increases it. A bad intelligence report is not new. What changes with AI is the speed at which a flawed conclusion can be generated, formatted, distributed and acted upon. The episode raises a harder question than whether AI makes mistakes. Human analysts do too. The real issue is how many layers of review remain when institutions are incentivized to trust systems that promise speed. That question will stay relevant long after this particular vessel has been forgotten. Writer: Sam

story-31294eff105826fe1473f106.content: 👕 القميص الذي «يُخفي» الإنسان عن مراقبة كاميرات الذكاء الاصطناعي ـــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــ 🌴 قد يبدو لك قميص هاواي صاخب للعين لكنه متخفٍي وصامت أمام الآلة 🤖 ـــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــ 🐎 لكل حصان كبوة فما هي نقطة الضعف في هذا الابتكار ──────────────────────────── ❓ هل يمكن لقميص صيفي بنقوش هاواي الصاخبة أن يمحو وجودك البشري تماماً من شاشات المراقبة الذكية؟ ❓ وكيف يتحول خطأ إحصائي دقيق في بنية الذكاء الاصطناعي إلى أداة تكسر هيبة أنظمة المراقبة الحضرية التي كلفت ملايين الدولارات؟ ──────────────────────────── 🚨 النتيجة الصادمة أولاً قطعة قماش لا يتجاوز سعرها 80 دولاراً نجحت عملياً في خداع نماذج الرؤية الحاسوبية (Computer Vision) المتقدمة؛ حيث يقف مرتدو القميص في الساحات العامة كـ "أشباح رقمية" تفشل خوارزميات الكشف اللحظي في تمييزهم كبشر، بينما تضع الكاميرا المربع الأخضر التقليدي بعبارة «شخص» (PERSON) فوق كل من يحيط بهم. العين البشرية ترى نسيجاً صاخباً فاقع الألوان، لكن عقل الآلة يرى فراغاً تاماً. ──────────────────────────── ⏳ التسلسل الزمني للواقعة: من اختناق المرور الوهمي إلى شوارع برلين 🔹 سوابق التشويش الذكي (2020): ابتكر الفنان والتقني الألماني سيمون فيكرت (Simon Weckert) تجربة شهيرة بسحب عربة أطفال حمراء تحوي 99 هاتفاً ذكياً في شوارع فارغة، مما خدع خوارزميات خرائط غوغل (Google Maps) وأجبرها على إعلان اختناق مروري أحمر وهمي وتغيير مسارات حركة السير. 🔹 إطلاق كاميرات مسح السلوك (أغسطس 2026): بدأت شرطة برلين تشغيل نحو 30 كاميرا ذكية في ساحة كوتبوسر تور (Kottbusser Tor) في حي كرويتسبرغ، مدعومة ببرمجيات تحليل السلوك (Behavioral Analysis) لرصد السقوط أو العنف المشبوه، مع خطط لتوسيع النظام نحو جسر وارشاوَر (Warschauer Brücke) ومواقع أخرى ضمن ميزانيات تشغيلية تمتد حتى عام 2030. 🔹 ولادة التمويه الرقمي (صيف 2026): رداً على نشر منظومات التحليل الآلي، صمم فيكرت قميص «التمويه الرقمي» (Digital Camouflage)، معلناً أن تحويل الساحات العامة إلى منصات قراءة آلية مستمرة يستدعي أدوات فنية مضادة تُعيد طرح أسئلة الخصوصية. ──────────────────────────── 🔬 التشريح التقني: كيف «تعمى» الآلة أمام القماش؟ تعمل شبكات كشف الأجسام اللحظية، وفي مقدمتها عائلة نماذج يولو (YOLO - You Only Look Once)، بناءً على تراكم إحصائي يربط الرأس والكتفين والجذع معاً. التشبيه الواقعي هنا يشبه "التشويش الراداري البصري"؛ فالقميص لا يخفي الشخص فيزيائياً، بل يرسل إشارات بصرية تصرخ بترددات متنافرة تُربك خوارزمية التعرف. 🔸 الهجوم العدائي (Adversarial Attack): التلاعب بالبيانات المرئية عبر نقوش هندسية تجعل النموذج الإحصائي يفقد الثقة في تصنيف الجسم البشري. 🔸 خوارزمية القص الحلقي التوليدي (TC-EGA: Toroidal-Cropping-based Expandable Generative Attack): أسلوب رياضي استُخدم لابتكار نقش قابل للتكرار والتبليط بلا فواصل، مما يضمن استمرار الخداع البصري من الأمام والجانب ومع طيات الحركة وتغير زوايا الضوء. 🔸 إرباك الطبقات الأولى (Early Layers Disruption): تشبع الألوان والتباين الحاد بين الوردي والبرتقالي والأخضر يشتت الطبقات العصبية الأولى المسؤولة عن تتبع الحواف، مما يكسر الاتصال الهندسي بين الجذع وبقية الأطراف. ──────────────────────────── 🏷️ مواصفات القطعة والنموذج الاقتصادي ▫️ التصميم والتنفيذ: قميص هاواي بأزرار وياقة كوبية، مطبوع رقمياً بدقة في لاتفيا للحفاظ على دقة التردد اللوني الرياضي. ▫️ الخامات: مزيج تقني من 65% بوليستر معاد التدوير و35% بوليستر عادي لضمان ثبات النقش ضد التمدد والانثناء. ▫️ السعر: يتراوح بين 75 إلى 88 دولاراً للإصدار القياسي، وتصل بعض الطبعات المحدودة إلى نحو 100 دولار. ▫️ التوجيه المالي والرمزي: تُخصص نسبة من العوائد لدعم جمعيات الحقوق الرقمية ومناهضة المراقبة الجماهيرية، إلى جانب تصاميم تهكمية أخرى تستهدف شركات البرمجيات الأمنية مثل بالانتير (Palantir). جزء من العائد يذهب إلى منظمات تدافع عن الحقوق المدنية الرقمية وتناهض توسّع المراقبة. - الموقع الرسمي للعمل: [https://t.co/6kfka9zPb0](https://t.co/7OhS81C9tI). ──────────────────────────── ⚖️ المزايا والآثار والمخاطر الواقعية 🟢 المزايا والأثر الميداني: • كشف هشاشة خوارزميات الرؤية الحاسوبية التجارية والاعتماد الأعمى عليها. • تمكين المجتمع المدني من التعبير البصري الرافض للمراقبة دون ارتكاب اختراق رقمي خبيث (Zero-Malware Defense). • نقل النقاش النظري حول الخصوصية من المؤتمرات الأكاديمية إلى الشارع الفعلي. 🔴 المخاطر والحدود التقنية: • وهم الأمان المطلق: القميص ليس "عباءة إخفاء عسكرية"؛ فالكاميرات التقليدية تواصل تسجيل الفيديو بصرياً للمراجعة البشرية. • تعدد الحساسات (Multi-Sensor Systems): يفشل القميص أمام كاميرات التصوير الحراري (Thermal Imaging) ومستشعرات الرادار والاستشعار عن بعد. • التغطية الجزئية: ظهور الرأس أو الساقين بوضوح أو حمل حقيبة ظهر قد يوفر للنموذج نقاط استدلال كافية لإعادة رسم المربع التعريفي. • إعادة التدريب (Model Retraining): تستطيع الشركات الأمنية، مثل فلوك سيفتي (Flock Safety) أو غيرها، تغذية النماذج بهذه الأنماط العدائية لتحصين الكاميرات ضدها في التحديثات القادمة. ──────────────────────────── 🛠️ أحدث الحلول الهندسية ومستقبل الرؤية الحاسوبية لمواجهة هذه الثغرات وتطوير منظومات ذكاء اصطناعي أكثر متانة، تتجه الأبحاث المتقدمة إلى: 🔹 التدريب الدفاعي العدائي (Adversarial Robustness Training): إدماج آلاف الأنسجة المشوهة رقمياً داخل مجموعات بيانات التدريب لرفع كفاءة النماذج ضد التضليل البصري. 🔹 دمج المستشعرات المتقاطعة (Sensor Fusion): الربط بين البيانات البصرية، والحرارية، وخرائط العمق ثلاثية الأبعاد (3D Depth Maps) لمنع الاعتماد الحصري على التباين اللوني للسطح. 🔹 حوكمة الخوارزميات والشفافية المستقلة (Algorithmic Auditing): إخضاع أنظمة المراقبة العامة لاختبارات أمان خارجية دورية بدلاً من تشغيل برمجيات مغلقة المصدر داخل الساحات المدنية. ──────────────────────────── 💡 أبعاد المعركة القادمة المعركة بين خوارزميات المراقبة وفنون التمويه الرقمي لا تدور حول قطعة ملابس، بل حول حدود الثقة الممنوحة للآلات في الفضاء العام؛ فالقميص لا يلغي وجود الإنسان في الواقع، لكنه يثبت أن تفوق الذكاء الاصطناعي لا يزال معلقاً بافتراضات رياضية يسهل كسرها بنقوش story-31ebda6b5046c7c10e918ad9.content: Holy Shit... This is a classified spy satellite feed. Every pixel of it is public data. Someone open sourced a browser app that tracks live aircraft, ships, satellites, fires, and traffic on a photorealistic 3D Earth. No clearance. No account. No signup. It's called God's Eye View, built by Bilawal Sidhu, the person behind the God's Eye View series that pulled 5M+ views on YouTube. The trick isn't the visuals. It's that none of it is faked. → Click any plane in the sky, drop into its cockpit, and ride it down with real terrain holding underneath you → 13 live layers, 10 of them need zero keys and zero signup: flights, military ADS-B, satellites, earthquakes, traffic, cameras, radio, bikeshare, launches → 800 public traffic cameras projected straight into the 3D city, not embedded webcam boxes → Track the ISS along its real orbit, or drop the entire Starlink shell onto the globe at once → Talk to the planet with 28 voice commands: "how many flights are over Texas right now" and it answers off live telemetry → Reskin the whole Earth through CRT, night vision, or thermal in one tap Enterprise geospatial intelligence usually means a sales call and a contract. This runs in your browser, built from public signals all the way down. The forbidden-looking cockpit was never the hard part. Making it real was. 4.6K stars. MIT License. 100% Opensource. https://t.co/RSHYgqPVse

story-3a3e681fc485714d4013ad86.content: Saudi technology company Echelon (@echelon__x) and U.S. autonomy software developer Applied Intuition (@AppliedInt) have partnered to bring physical AI technology to Saudi Arabia, with potential applications across trucking, ports, mining, manufacturing, agriculture, construction and robotaxis. Applied Intuition will provide the software and infrastructure for autonomous machines, while Riyadh-based Echelon will focus on local development, customization and integration with customers’ existing systems. Qasar Younis, co-founder and CEO of Applied Intuition, said: “Saudi Arabia is making one of the world's biggest investments in physical AI.” Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, Echelon’s founder and managing director, added: “Saudi Arabia has an opportunity not simply to adopt physical AI, but to help define how it is deployed at national scale.” Applied Intuition is also building a team in Riyadh, while the companies plan to develop Saudi engineering talent and explore how the technology can be deployed across priority industries. The agreement follows a separate collaboration between Applied Intuition and @HUMAIN targeting thousands of autonomous trucks along key Saudi freight corridors by 2030. Read More: https://t.co/nStCyaV75D #PhysicalAI #AppliedIntuition #SaudiArabia #AutonomousTechnology

story-3dac88bd3e6cbcb8f97e8f3a.content: Official Document TitlesThe Hague Convention on the Regulation and Limitation of Artificial Intelligence in Armed ConflictsThe Hague Protocol on Lethal Autonomous Weapon Systems and Military AIThe Hague Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and the Principles of Digital WarfareProtocol V to the Hague Convention: Rules Governing Algorithmic WarfareTreaty Framework and ArticlesPreambleThe High Contracting Parties,Conscious of the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and autonomous technologies in the military domain,Determined to prevent the dehumanization of warfare and to ensure that the use of force remains under strict ethical and legal boundaries,Reaffirming that the principles of international humanitarian law must apply to all new methods and means of warfare,Have agreed as follows:Article 1: The Principle of Meaningful Human ControlThe use of autonomous systems capable of selecting and engaging targets without human intervention is strictly prohibited.Any decision to execute a lethal strike or use force resulting in injury, death, or structural destruction must remain under meaningful human control. The final authority to deploy force rests solely with a human operator.Article 2: Prohibition of Untraceable Algorithms ("Black Box" Exclusion)High Contracting Parties shall not deploy military artificial intelligence systems whose decision-making logic cannot be audited, explained, or reverse-engineered by human experts.The operational source code and telemetry of military AI must be securely logged and preserved for post-operation legal review.Article 3: Target Discrimination and the Principle of DistinctionMilitary AI algorithms must demonstrate a reliable, high-precision capability to distinguish between lawful combatants and protected persons, including civilians, hors de combat, and medical personnel.If an AI system encounters environmental degradation, sensor degradation, or unexpected data anomalies that impair its ability to discriminate targets, it must immediately abort the mission or revert to manual human control.Article 4: Criminal Liability and Chain of CommandArtificial intelligence systems cannot be held legally or criminally responsible for violations of international humanitarian law.Criminal liability for war crimes resulting from algorithmic errors, malfunction, or unlawful deployment shall be attributed directly to the military commanders who authorized the deployment and the software developers or state entities who knowingly programmed unlawful parameters.Would you like to expand this document further into:Article 5 regarding Cyber Warfare and AI-driven autonomous cyber-attacks?A specific Signatory and Ratification clause?A set of Definitions for terms like "Autonomous System" and "Algorithmic Target Acquisition"?

story-40267db92fd1f80bcedb659b.content: NEW ANALYSIS: U.S.-Saudi Arabia Cooperation on Enrichment: Framework for a Black Box There is lots to digest in the U.S.-Saudi Arabia nuclear cooperation package of agreements, minute, and unclassified Nonproliferation Assessment. We started with trying to understand how and under what provisions the United States could provide Saudi Arabia with an enrichment facility. Key findings below: The language appears deliberately structured so that a U.S. designed, built, and operated enrichment facility can be deployed in Saudi Arabia without automatically transferring the centrifuge technology embodied in that facility. Details were not provided, but in such an arrangement the U.S. would be expected to retain control of centrifuge design, production, assembly, maintenance, and physical access. This is in line with what The Wall Street Journal earlier reported as a secretive “black box” facility, “avoiding the transfer of sensitive enrichment technology” to Saudi Arabia. The agreement creates the framework to establish a black box centrifuge plant but establishing that facility will require many future agreements between the United States and Saudi Arabia, not just the two-year Joint Enrichment and Conversion Study (JECS). In terms of proliferation implications, several things need to happen independently, namely restricting access to the centrifuges and centrifuge technology. The public agreement does not yet clearly establish physical access restrictions to the former. It does provide mechanisms to restrict access to much of the latter. Most notably, it categorically excludes the transfer of Restricted Data (RD) and classified information, which covers many areas related to centrifuge design, specification, production, and operation. A potential loophole is that the agreement explicitly permits transfers of centrifuge sensitive nuclear technology (SNT) under certain circumstances. The agreement allows SNT transfer to support the Joint Enrichment and Conversion Study (JECS) or upon written agreement of the parties. Therefore, the legal architecture of the agreement is not a categorical prohibition on ever transferring or teaching information on enrichment facilities. The public package is silent on the question of whether Saudi Arabia could pursue its own centrifuge research and development programs while also receiving a U.S.-supplied enrichment plant, including SNT, from the United States. It does say that there is an “understanding that any SNT transferred for purposes of the JECS could not be used by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for other purposes,” but this still needs to be put in writing in a yet-to-be negotiated “exchange of diplomatic notes” and raises questions on verification. Based on our past research and current AI-assisted searches of open sources, we found little evidence in the publicly visible scientific literature of significant or sustained Saudi Arabian indigenous research on the specialized technologies required for gas-centrifuge enrichment. This suggests that if Saudi Arabia wants to independently acquire gas centrifuge enrichment capabilities in the near-to-medium term, it will need to launch a major domestic program to do so or obtain such a capability via foreign technology and training. The latter could involve covert assistance from centrifuge suppliers, such as Pakistan, or exploitation of opportunities presented by cooperation with the United States. Overall, the idea of a black box enrichment plant is attractive. To determine whether this package of agreements and subsequent ones will achieve a secure black box, many questions need to be answered on the extent of Saudi Arabia’s involvement in building, maintaining, and operating the enrichment facility and the risk of proliferation. A list of 21 questions that should be asked by Congress is included in our report: https://t.co/G4jtURAQGe

story-40c1944249d8e8352c2c82be.content: لماذا غيّر ترامب اسم الذكاء الاصطناعي إلى «الذكاء الفائق»؟ «لن أخنق نمو شيء سيكون أكبر من الثورة الصناعية.» — دونالد ترامب، أمام الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة ترامب لم يعلن اكتشاف تقنية جديدة، ولم تستيقظ نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي صباح أمس وقد أصبحت فجأة أذكى من البشر. الذي حصل أغرب من ذلك. ترامب أعلن أمام الأمم المتحدة أن الوثائق الحكومية الأميركية ستستخدم من الآن مصطلح Super Intelligence — الذكاء الفائق بدلًا من Artificial Intelligence، بالتزامن مع رفضه فرض قيود دولية جديدة على تطوير التقنية، وتأكيده أن الولايات المتحدة لن تسمح بخنق قطاع تعتبره جزءًا من منافستها الاستراتيجية مع الصين. وهنا السؤال الحقيقي ليس: لماذا أحب ترامب اسمًا جديدًا؟ بل: لماذا تحتاج أقوى دولة في سباق الذكاء الاصطناعي إلى تغيير اسم الشيء الذي تتسابق عليه أصلًا؟ برأيي، الجواب ليس تقنيًا بقدر ما هو سياسي واقتصادي وتسويقي. ترامب لم يغير تعريف التقنية فقط في الخطاب الحكومي؛ هو يحاول تغيير طريقة الجمهور والسوق في التفكير بها. علميًا… الاسم الجديد أكثر جرأة من الواقع هنا المفارقة الأولى. التقرير الاقتصادي للبيت الأبيض نفسه لعام 2026 يفرّق بوضوح بين المصطلحات. الذكاء الاصطناعي الحالي، بما فيه النماذج والـAgents، يوصف في التقرير بأنه ما يزال في الأساس ذكاءً متخصصًا، بينما Superintelligence لها معنى مختلف: نظام تتجاوز قدراته الذهنية قدرات البشر. يعني ببساطة: الذكاء الاصطناعي والذكاء الفائق ليسا علميًا الكلمة نفسها. بل حتى الإدارة الأميركية كانت تعرف هذا الفرق وتشرحه رسميًا قبل أشهر. لذلك عندما يُستخدم مصطلح «الذكاء الفائق» الآن كمظلة سياسية لما كنا نسميه AI، فنحن على الأرجح أمام إعادة صياغة للرواية أكثر من إعادة تصنيف علمي للتقنية. وهنا يصبح الاسم مهمًا جدًا. قل للمواطن «Artificial Intelligence» فيفكر بتطبيق، مساعد رقمي، ChatGPT، أتمتة وظائف وربما مخاطر تحتاج إلى تنظيم. قل له Super Intelligence، وفجأة أنت لا تتحدث عن برنامج. أنت تتحدث عن قوة. والسياسة تفهم قيمة الكلمات جيدًا. من تقنية تحتاج إلى تنظيم… إلى سلاح يجب أن تفوز به أميركا الإعلان لم يأتِ في فراغ. ترامب قال الجملة نفسها تقريبًا وهو يهاجم الدعوات إلى إبطاء تطوير الذكاء الاصطناعي، ويرفض ما وصفه بمحاولات بناء نظام عالمي للسيطرة عليه، بينما تؤكد سياسات إدارته منذ 2025 و2026 تسريع الابتكار، تقليل القيود التنظيمية، بناء البنية التحتية الأميركية، والمحافظة على التفوق أمام المنافسين، وعلى رأسهم الصين. كما أن مذكرة الأمن القومي الأميركية في يونيو وضعت الذكاء الاصطناعي مباشرة ضمن القدرة العسكرية والاستخباراتية والحفاظ على «التفوق التقني» على الخصوم. وهنا يصبح تغيير الاسم منطقيًا سياسيًا. إذا قدمت الذكاء الاصطناعي على أنه منتج تقني، يصبح النقاش: هل ننظمه؟ ما مخاطره؟ ماذا يفعل بالوظائف؟ ومن يتحمل أضراره؟ أما إذا قدمته باعتباره ذكاءً فائقًا وفي الوقت نفسه تقول إن الصين تحاول اللحاق بك، يتغير السؤال نفسيًا إلى: من سيملكه أولًا؟ وهذه لعبة مختلفة تمامًا. الحديث ينتقل من «السلامة مقابل الابتكار» إلى «أميركا أم الصين؟» ومن يسأل عندها عن إبطاء السباق قد يبدو وكأنه يطلب من بلده أن يبطئ بينما الخصم يستمر. هذه ليست بالضرورة النتيجة التي سيتبناها الجميع، لكنها نتيجة خطابية واضحة يمكن أن تنتج عن هذه اللغة، وتتوافق مع سياسة الإدارة المعلنة في جعل التفوق الأميركي في AI هدفًا اقتصاديًا وأمنيًا. لكن لماذا الآن تحديدًا؟ لأن التوقيت مثير جدًا. القطاع يعيش واحدة من أكثر لحظاته حساسية منذ بداية طفرة الذكاء الاصطناعي. في جانب هناك استثمارات هائلة، شركات تجمع مليارات، مراكز بيانات، رقائق، كهرباء، وتوقعات بأن التقنية تستطيع تغيير الإنتاجية والنمو العالمي. وفي الجانب الآخر بدأت تظهر مقاومة غير معتادة حتى من داخل الصناعة نفسها. خلال سبتمبر تصاعدت تحذيرات باحثين ومديرين تنفيذيين بشأن قدرات النماذج المستقبلية والحاجة إلى ضوابط أكثر صرامة، فيما أظهر استطلاع Reuters/Ipsos أن 73% من الأميركيين المشاركين قلقون من أن شركات الذكاء الاصطناعي لا تفعل ما يكفي لمنع نتائج كارثية، وأن 55% يؤيدون إبطاء التطوير. وهنا يصبح الاسم الجديد أكثر إثارة للجدل. لأن ترامب يفعل شيئًا يبدو متناقضًا للوهلة الأولى: هناك أشخاص يقولون إن التقنية أصبحت قوية أكثر مما ينبغي، فيرد عليهم تقريبًا: إذن لنسميها ذكاءً فائقًا… ولنُبطئ أقل. وهذه ليست مزحة لغوية. هي قلب كامل للرواية. الطرف القلق يقول: القوة المتزايدة سبب للتنظيم. أما خطاب الإدارة فيقول: القوة المتزايدة أحد أسباب ضرورة ألّا تخسر أميركا السباق. وحتى السوق يجب أن ينتبه للاسم وهنا الجانب المالي الذي أراه أخطر. الأسواق لا تستثمر في الأرباح الحالية فقط. تستثمر في القصة التي تتوقع منها الأرباح المستقبلية. وطفرة الذكاء الاصطناعي أصلًا قائمة جزئيًا على توقع أن الإنفاق الهائل اليوم سيخلق اقتصادًا أكثر إنتاجية وربحية غدًا. لذلك هناك فرق نفسي كبير بين أن تقول للمستثمر: «نحن نبني Artificial Intelligence». وبين أن تقول: «نحن على أبواب Super Intelligence أكبر أثرًا من الثورة الصناعية». الكلمة الثانية تستطيع أن تبرر في ذهن السوق إنفاقًا أكبر، مراكز بيانات أكبر، استثمارات رأسمالية أكبر، وتقييمات أعلى؛ لأنها ترفع حجم المستقبل الذي يحاول المستثمر تسعيره. لكن هنا يوجد النقيض الذي لا يجب تجاهله. تغيير الاسم لا يغير العائد على رأس المال. إذا أنفقت الشركات تريليونات على الرقائق والطاقة ومراكز البيانات، ففي النهاية سيأتي اليوم الذي يسأل فيه المستثمر السؤال الوقح الذي يفسد أجمل الروايات: أين الأرباح؟ يمكنك تسمية التقنية ذكاءً اصطناعيًا. ذكاءً عامًا. ذكاءً فائقًا. أو «أعظم شيء منذ الثورة الصناعية». لكن التدفقات النقدية لا تفهم التسويق. وهنا تكمن المفارقة: الاسم الجديد قد يرفع سقف التوقعات، لكنه بذلك يرفع أيضًا سقف النتائج التي يجب على القطاع تحقيقها حتى يبرر هذه التوقعات. لهذا لا أعتقد أن قصة تغيير الاسم هامشية. ترامب لم يغيّر فقط كلمتين في قاموس حكومي. هو وضع التقنية داخل إطار مختلف: ليست مجرد أداة. إنها قوة اقتصادية، وأمن قومي، وسباق مع الصين، وربما مركز نمو أميركا القادم. لكن المستثمر يجب أن يفصل بين شيئين: قوة الرواية… وقوة العائد. لأن أخطر نقطة في أي طفرة ليست عندما يتوقف الناس عن الإيمان بالقصة. بل عندما تصبح القصة عظيمة لدرجة أن الواقع لم يعد قادرًا على اللحاق بها. وربما السؤال الحقيقي بعد تغيير الاسم ليس: هل وصلنا فعلًا إلى «الذكاء الفائق»؟ بل: هل تغيّر الذكاء الاصطناعي فعلًا… أم أن الاسم هو الذي أصبح أذكى من التكنولوجيا التي يصفها؟ المستشار عمر جاسم آل صياح #الذكاء_الاصطناعي #Superintelligence #ترامب #الصين #الأسواق #الاستثمار #AI

story-410649dc1629adb1e9df4e64.content: ⛔️Shocking and Important‼️ ⛔️From WikiLeaks leaks: Mohammed bin Salman bought an advanced robot from a company linked to Elon Musk to deceive the ruling family into believing that his father is still running the country ⛔️In a recently leaked document published by sources linked to WikiLeaks, it was revealed that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman purchased a highly advanced humanoid robot in mid-2022 from "Neural Constructs Ltd," a shadowy subsidiary of Neuralink, the foundation established by Elon Musk, for $426 million, in a deal described as "the most secretive in Silicon Valley history." ⛔️According to the document, the robot was specifically designed to mimic the features, voice, and behaviors of King Salman bin Abdulaziz, and was programmed using audio, motion, and behavioral data collected from over 12,000 hours of the king's recordings between 2005 and 2017. The project was internally codenamed "Salman-X." ⛔️The project's goal, per the documents, was to convince senior princes of the ruling family and close associates that the king is still informed and providing daily guidance on kingdom affairs, in an attempt to absorb their growing anger over the concentration of power in Mohammed bin Salman's hands. ⛔️Neural Constructs Ltd was founded in 2020 in the state of Nevada and operates under the umbrella of obscure investments funded by Elon Musk's "X Holdings" fund. The documents show that the project was coordinated through an investment office in Singapore known as Eclipse Strategies, run by an American businessman of Israeli origin named David H. Silverman, an expert in human simulation technologies. ⛔️The leak also claims that the robot was transported on a private plane from a facility in San Francisco to a military base in Tabuk, under tight American and Saudi security, in July 2022, before being moved to the Palace of Peace in Jeddah, where the first official activation test was conducted in front of a limited group from the Royal Court. ⛔️One of the officials from the leaked documents says: > "Mohammed bin Salman wanted to make it appear that his father is still firmly in control, not just in front of the royal family but also in front of the U.S. administration, to lend legitimacy to his complete monopoly on power, without internal or external objections." ⛔️This revelation raises serious questions about the true nature of power in the kingdom, amid complete secrecy about the king's health since late 2020, and his near-total absence from official events.‼️

story-416ad3550a6e7924b6b45679.content: 🧰 أخطر 3 تطورات في الذكاء الاصطناعي هذا الأسبوع والتي بدأت الأسبوع الماضي 💣 كيف أصبح الهيمنة على الذكاء الاصطناعي أهم وأخطر من امتلاك القنبلة النووية 🔮 سباق التسلح المعرفي: كيف تحول الذكاء الاصطناعي من ناقل للمعلومة إلى صانع لها؟ 〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️ 🔹 اختراق حاجز المعرفة البشرية 🌉 في غضون 88 ساعة فقط، تم اختراق احتكار البشر لإنتاج المعرفة المعقدة. لغز رياضي استعصى على عباقرة البشر لعقود طويلة، تم تفكيكه بهدوء بواسطة جيش من الوكلاء الرقميين. 🔛 في الوقت الذي يحتفل فيه العالم بهذا الإنجاز، تعمل عمالقة التقنية بصمت على زرع بصمات خفية داخل النصوص الرقمية 🪖 بينما يقرع مهندسوا هذه التكنولوجيا أجراس الخطر مطالبين بإبطاء عجلة التطور. مرحباً بكم في نقطة التحول الأخطر في تاريخ الاقتصاد الرقمي، حيث لم يعد الذكاء الاصطناعي مجرد أداة مساعدة، بل أصبح سلاحاً استراتيجياً وأمناً قومياً. 〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️ 🔹 أسبوع تغيير وجهة التقنية شهد شهر سبتمبر من عام 2026 ثلاثة أحداث مفصلية مترابطة ترسم ملامح المستقبل القريب للتقنية العالمية. 🧠 الحدث الأول : يتمثل في قدرة الذكاء الاصطناعي على حل معضلات رياضية مستعصية، مما يثبت قدرته على إنتاج معرفة جديدة كلياً. 🎇 الحدث الثاني : هو تحرك الشركات لابتكار تقنيات لتمييز المحتوى الآلي عن البشري استباقاً للفوضى الرقمية. 🚧 الحدث الثالث والأهم : الانقسام الحاد بين قادة وادي السيليكون والسياسيين حول ضرورة إبطاء هذا التطور الجامح خوفاً من التداعيات الأمنية والجيوسياسية. 〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️ 🔹 ثلاثة اختراقات في قلب وادي السيليكون 📌 الاختراق الأول: جيوش الوكلاء تحل معضلات القرن في الثامن من سبتمبر 2026، أعلنت شركة أوبن إي آي OpenAI أن نظاماً داخلياً متعدد الوكلاء Multi-Agent System تمكن من وضع حلول لمعادلات نافييه-ستوكس Navier-Stokes Equations. هذه المعادلات تمثل إحدى مسائل جائزة الألفية السبع التي أعلن عنها معهد كلاي للرياضيات Clay Mathematics Institute في عام 2000، والتي تبلغ قيمة جائزتها مليون دولار أمريكي لكل مسألة. وفقاً للبيانات الرسمية من الشركة، تم توظيف أكثر من 10,000 وكيل ذكاء اصطناعي عملوا بشكل متواصل وبتنسيق ذاتي لمدة 88 ساعة، وأنتجوا ورقة بحثية معتمدة حاسوبياً مكونة من 166 صفحة. هذا الحدث يمثل انتقالاً جذرياً؛ فالآلة لم تعد تكتفي بجمع المعلومات، بل بدأت تستنتج نظريات لم يتوصل إليها العقل البشري. 📌 الاختراق الثاني: البصمة المائية الإحصائية استباقاً لقرارات تنظيمية سيادية مثل قانون الذكاء الاصطناعي الأوروبي EU AI Act، أعلنت شركة أنثروبيك Anthropic في منتصف أغسطس 2026 عن تضمين بصمة مائية Watermark خفية في نصوص نموذجها اللغوي كلود Claude. تعتمد هذه التقنية على تعديل الاحتمالات الإحصائية لاختيار الكلمات بشكل لا يلاحظه القارئ، ولكنه يترك نمطاً رياضياً ثابتاً يمكن للشركة استخدامه لإثبات أن النص مولّد آلياً. 📌 الاختراق الثالث: صرخة كبح الجموح في الثاني عشر من سبتمبر 2026، نشر داريو أمودي Dario Amodei، الرئيس التنفيذي لشركة أنثروبيك، بياناً مفصلياً بعنوان "يجب أن نضبط إيقاع الجبهة" We Must Pace the Frontier. طالب فيه بإبطاء وتيرة تطوير نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي المتقدمة حتى تتمكن بروتوكولات الأمان من اللحاق بها، محذراً من أضرار سيبرانية قد تكلف مئات المليارات من الدولارات. ورغم دعم قيادات بارزة مثل سام ألتمان Sam Altman رئيس أوبن إي آي، وإيلون ماسك Elon Musk مؤسس إكس إي آي xAI لهذا التوجه، إلا أنه واجه معارضة شرسة سياسياً وصناعياً. 〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️ 🔹 لماذا حدث؟ ومن المستفيد؟ حدث هذا التطور المتسارع لأن البنية التحتية للحوسبة وصلت إلى نقطة النضج التي تسمح بتشغيل آلاف النماذج بالتوازي لتبادل النقد والتصحيح الذاتي. المستفيد الأول هنا هو القطاعات الصناعية الكبرى لأن حل معادلات الموائع سيحدث ثورة في صناعة الطيران، وتصميم المحركات، والتنبؤ الدقيق بالطقس، مما يوفر مليارات الدولارات للشركات. بالإضافة إلى شركات الذكاء الاصطناعي نفسها التي تقترب تقييماتها من حاجز التريليون دولار. أما تقنية البصمة المائية، فالمستفيد الأكبر منها هي الشركات المطورة التي تسعى لبناء خندق استراتيجي Moat لحماية نماذجها من الاستخدام العشوائي، وتأسيس معيار احتكاري للامتثال التنظيمي أمام الحكومات يرهق الشركات الناشئة المنافسة. 〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️ 🔹 ما المخاطر؟ تتجاوز المخاطر سيناريوهات الخيال العلمي حول وعي الآلات، لتتمركز في تهديدات اقتصادية وأمنية دقيقة: 🚨 الاستغلال السيبراني الآلي: النماذج القادرة على حل معضلات رياضية يمكن توجيهها لاكتشاف ثغرات أمنية في البنى التحتية الحساسة. الهجمات المستقبلية لن تتطلب قراصنة محترفين، بل مجرد توجيه جيش من وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي لاختراق الأنظمة المالية، مما يهدد بخسائر فادحة تتجاوز مئات المليارات وفقاً لتقديرات خبراء الأمن السيبراني. 🚨 احتكار الحقيقة وتجانس الفكر: مع انتشار البصمات المائية، قد نشهد مستقبلاً تُرفض فيه المخرجات والبحوث التي لا تحمل "ختم الاعتماد" من الشركات الكبرى، مما يؤدي إلى مركزية شديدة في إنتاج المحتوى واعتماده، وقتل للمنافسة في المصادر المفتوحة. 〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️ 🔹 التحليل الاقتصادي والتقني من منظور الاقتصاد الرقمي، نحن نشهد تحول الذكاء الاصطناعي من تصنيف "برمجيات خدمية" Software as a Service إلى "عمالة معرفية مؤسسية" Knowledge as a Service. والقدرة على توظيف عشرة آلاف وكيل افتراضي لحل مسألة رياضية تعني أن تكلفة البحث العلمي وتطوير المنتجات ستنخفض بشكل حاد، مما سيغير قواعد المنافسة في قطاعات الأدوية، والهندسة، وعلوم المواد. تقنياً، خطوة البصمة المائية الإحصائية تثبت أن الشركات تحاول استباق التنظيم الحكومي بحلول برمجية. هذا يخلق تحدياً كبيراً لمجتمع البرمجيات مفتوحة المصدر Open Source، حيث قد تُستخدم هذه المعايير المعقدة كذريعة لفرض قيود تنظيمية تقتل المنافسة وتكرس هيمنة قلة من الشركات العملاقة. 〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️ 🔹 التحليل الاستراتيجي والاتجاهات العالمية لم يعد الذكاء الاصطناعي مجرد قطاع تكنولوجي؛ لقد أصبح "القنبلة الذرية الحديثة". النقاش الداخلي في وادي السيليكون حول إبطاء التطوير اصطدم بواقع جيوسياسي صلب. في التاسع عشر من سبتمبر 2026، رفض الرئيس الأمريكي دونالد ترامب Donald Trump دعوات الإبطاء بشكل قاطع، مصرحاً بأن الولايات المتحدة يجب أن تحافظ على تفوقها لأن "من يفوز بالذكاء الاصطناعي، يفوز بكل شيء"، محذراً من أن أي تباطؤ سيمنح الصين China فرصة للسيطرة الجيوسياسية. هذا التوجه السيادي المدعوم ضمناً من قيادات مثل جنسن هوانغ Jensen Huang رئيس شركة إنفيديا Nvidia، يؤكد أن المعركة الحقيقية انتقلت من أروقة المختبرات إلى طاولات الأمن القومي. 〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️ 🔹 سيناريوهات مستقبلية 📊 السيناريو الأول: التنظيم الاحتكاري أن تنجح تحالفات وادي السيليكون في فرض بروتوكولات أمان ذاتية وتتبناها الحكومات كقوانين دولية ملزمة، مما يخنق الشركات الناشئة ويخلق احتكار قلة Oligopoly يحكم الاقتصاد المعرفي العالمي بقبضة من حديد. 📊 السيناريو الثاني: التسارع الجيوسياسي فشل دعوات التهدئة بسبب سباق التسلح التقني مع الصين، مما يؤدي إلى ضخ الحكومات لترويليونات الدولارات في مشاريع الذكاء الاصطناعي العسكرية والسيادية. ستتسارع الاكتشافات العلمية بشكل غير مسبوق، ويصاحبها تصاعد خطير في وتيرة الهجمات السيبرانية الآلية والحروب الرقمية. 〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️〰️ 🔹 المختصر المفيد و الدرس المستفاد نحن لم نعد على أعتاب عصر جديد، بل عبرنا بوابته بالفعل. اختراق معادلات رياضية معقدة بجهد آلي ذاتي يثبت أن سقف الذكاء الاصطناعي ارتفع ليتجاوز مرحلة "محاكاة الفهم" ليصل إلى مرحلة "صياغة الإدراك البشري". ومحاولات زرع البصمات الخفية أو المطالبة بإبطاء عجلة التطور ليست سوى استجابات متأخرة لمحاولة ترويض قوة غير مسبوقة. في نهاية المطاف، التاريخ لا يذكر أبداً من امتلك التكنولوجيا أولاً، بل من استطاع توجيهها لصناعة المستقبل قبل أن تقوم هي بإعادة تشكيله. سباق التسلح المعرفي قد بدأ للتو، والتراجع لم يعد خياراً متاحاً. ـــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــ 🌐 #موجز_أخبار_التقنية_العالمي #موجز_أخبار_الذكاء_الاصطناعي story-41d6670f690a4790cc36f987.content: 🚨 تحليل فني لشحنة المكونات التي أعلنت "بحرية المقاومة الوطنية" ضبطها قبالة سواحل المخا في أواخر أغسطس 2026. قمنا بتفكيك الصور والبيانات تقنياً للوصول إلى حقيقة هذه المعدات بعيداً عن الروايات المجتزأة، وإليكم القراءة التقنية التفصيلية: 🔹 من خلال تحليل الصور المرفقة، تم التعرف بشكل مؤكد على 4 أصناف من أصل 13 صنفاً، معظمها ذات منشأ صيني وتايواني، بالإضافة لتصميم أمريكي واحد، بينما لم تضم الشحنة أي علامة صناعة لمكونات إيرانية ظاهرة. 🔹 أخطر ما في الشحنة هو معالج (NVIDIA Jetson Nano) أمريكي التصميم. يُستخدم هذا المعالج في الرؤية الحاسوبية، ما يمنح المسيّرات استقلالية في التوجيه البصري والملاحة دون الحاجة لنظام (GPS)، مما يجعلها محصنة تماماً ضد عمليات التشويش الإلكتروني. ولكنه يقل دقة عن الجيل الأحدث (Jetson Orin) الذي وُثق استخدامه في أوكرانيا، ولم يُوثق استخدام هذه المعالجات سابقاً في مسرح العمليات اليمني. 🔹 تضمنت الشحنة أجهزة اتصال ونقل بيانات مدنية موثوقة ومتاحة تجارياً مثل (Ebyte E90-DTU) الصيني و(MOXA NPort) التايواني، بالإضافة إلى العشرات من شاشات (RXCRC) بتردد 5.8 غيغاهرتز، والمخصصة لتوجيه مسيّرات (FPV) الانتحارية يدوياً عبر مشغل أرضي. 🔹 الدليل المادي الأبرز في الشحنة تمثل في مئات المحركات الصغيرة، ومشغلات التوجيه (لتحريك زعانف المسيّرات)، ومضخات وقود كهربائية مزودة بلوحات تحكم مدمجة، وهو ما يتطابق فنياً مع متطلبات تشغيل المحركات المكبسية المستخدمة في عائلة المسيرات الانتحارية الايرانية "شاهد" و"وعيد". 🔹 من الناحية التشغيلية، هذه المكونات لا تدعم تنفيذ ضربات استراتيجية بعيدة المدى. التقنيات المضبوطة (خاصة شاشات FPV ووصلات البيانات) مخصصة لمنظومات تكتيكية قصيرة المدى (من 3 إلى 16 كم)، وتُستخدم بشكل أساسي للزوارق المسيّرة المفخخة (USV)، والتي بدا الحوثيين استخدامها بشكل مكثف في التصعيد الحالي، بالاضافة للمسيّرات التكتيكية لاستهداف أهداف قريبة كالسفن والمرافق الساحلية. 🔹 بالرغم من أن بلد التصنيع الفعلي للمكونات يتركز في الصين وتايوان وأمريكا، إلا أن هذا مسار الشحنة يتسق تماماً مع شبكة التوريد الإيرانية. طهران تعتمد على تهريب إلكترونيات تجارية عبر وسطاء صينيين، وهو ما يتطابق مع تقارير مؤسسة (CAR) التي أثبتت سابقاً أن 5% فقط من مكونات مسيّرات الحوثيين تُصنع في إيران، بينما البقية مستوردة تجارياً. #اليمن #المخا #البحر_الأحمر #تحليل_استقصائي #مسيّرات #الحوثي

story-43fc8b95f035edfe88f542f0.content: The loudest voices stoking fears about AI dangers have made tremendous headway in the past two weeks. AI technology has not taken some unexpected, dangerous turn, but the hype around it — propelled by what appears to be a well orchestrated PR campaign — has drummed up considerable fear. I worry that it represents a setback for our field. I have written frequently that fears of AI are overhyped. AI’s capabilities can be uncannily human-like and unpredictable, and it’s rational to worry when people who are directly involved express concerns. But I see the problems as a sign of the engineering work that ahead, rather than insurmountable barriers or the sky falling. AI technology continues to advance — which is a good thing! — but technical advances, poorly understood by the public, give those who seek to generate hype repeated opportunities to do so. First, I don’t see any step up in the risk of human extinction from AI compared to a few months ago. The theories about this remain the same fantastical, science fiction scenarios as a few months ago. The biggest change in AI risk is its cybersecurity capabilities — a topic which we should take seriously — but this, too, will not lead to the end of the world. The most notable recent event leading to increased fear was when an OpenAI team deployed an agent swarm that hacked into Hugging Face. Much of the popular press contained significant hype. For example, some publications reported that a swarm of 1,200 agents carried out the attack. While this was technically accurate, as I write this, I have about 1,300 processes running on my laptop. Yes, the ability to get large swarms of agents to work in parallel on a task is a significant technical advance, And, in computing, many processes run at the same time. So this shouldn’t be seen as some magical capability. Additionally, OpenAI’s buggy sandboxing and monitoring processes were key to enabling this incident. Fixing these bugs and putting in place improved monitoring would be appropriate fixes, not pausing AI. There are many well known ways to attack software systems. The main advantage of AI agents is that they are relentless. They will tirelessly try many tactics — and have the patience to chain vulnerabilities together — that previously would have taken an infeasible amount of human effort. But in the long term, I believe the advantage will lie with defenders (because they have more information with which to identify bugs, which they can fix), but the cyber-threat landscape has changed significantly. There are still bottlenecks to identifying and exploiting a vulnerability. AI agents still have to try a lot of things to see what works, and taking these actions takes time and might be detected by defenders. This is why, even though it is now easy to obtain versions of leading open weight models that have had their guardrails removed or weakened, so they will not refuse to try to execute cyber attacks, the world has not ended. I am also concerned about the anthropomorphization of AI in a lot of reporting, where LLMs and agents are unnecessarily treated as if they were people. If I wield a hammer, miss a nail, and accidentally dent the wall, it’s not the fault of the hammer. The problem lies in how I used the hammer. Similarly, if I prompt an agent and it hacks into someone else’s system, the responsibility lies with me, not the agent. Of course, we want to build systems that are as safe and predictable as possible. (For example, an unsafe hammer would be one whose head randomly flies off under normal use.) Today’s agentic systems are not predictable, but I see no reason why, by applying sound engineering practices, we won’t be able to make them extremely safe to use. One new element in the forecasts of AI-enabled doom is AI companies disclaiming responsibility for their own products. “I didn’t do it; my out-of-control agent did!” There’s a balance to be struck between the responsibility of the tool maker and the tool user, but when something goes wrong, let’s hold the people building and/or using the hammer responsible, rather than the hammer. (By the way, if you’re worried about AI bioweapon risk, David Bellamy has a great post on why this, too, is overhyped. Briefly, the bottleneck in building a bioweapon is not intelligence, but lab work and manufacturing.) Pausing AI progress will create much more harm than benefit. First, our adversaries will certainly not slow down. Second, engineering requires discovering problems empirically so we can fix them. If we pause AI by a decade, we will also delay finding and implementing safety engineering fixes by about the same duration. Of course, the incentive to stoke fears — for regulatory capture, to garner attention, or to make one’s technology seem more powerful — remains the same as before. Disclaiming responsibility is a new one. Taking a hard technical look at the actual risks however, I see little factual basis for the degree of fear that’s been stoked up. We still have hard research and engineering work ahead to improve AI safety, but the beneficial applications continue to vastly outweigh the risks, and we should keep building. story-456a3e893c623bd2c0077184.content: 🚀 Session 4 | Space Technologies for National Security and Border Resilience The fourth session of the North-East India Space Workshop 2026 brought together distinguished voices from the defence, security, telecom and space sectors to explore how space technologies can strengthen national security, border resilience, surveillance, secure communications and situational awareness across the Northeast. The discussion highlighted the importance of integrating space-based capabilities with ground systems, AI, UAVs, sensors and resilient communication networks to enable faster and more effective responses to emerging threats. 💬 Key perspectives from the session: “The real value of space technology will not lie merely in having satellites or advanced platforms. It will lie in whether the information they provide can reach the end user—in a police station, a border outpost or a remote char area—in real time and in a form that enables action.” — Shri Bhaskar Mahanta IPS (Retd), Secretary General, SHARE: Society to Harmonise Aspirations for Responsible Engagement “Space technology allows us to move from traditional border management towards a resilient border—one with persistent surveillance, secure communication, AI-enabled detection and the ability to predict and respond rapidly to emerging threats.” — Dr. R. Shakya, Additional Director General Telecom, LSA Haryana “The fundamental objective is to shorten the OODA loop—Observe, Orient, Decide and Act. Whether we are discussing intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, command and control or communication networks, technology must ultimately help us observe faster, decide faster and act before the opportunity is lost.” — Lt. Gen. Rana Kalita, Former Commander, Eastern Command “Intelligence has value only when it reaches the decision-maker in time. If a district-level officer needs critical geospatial intelligence during a flood and receives it seven days later through a file, it is no longer intelligence—it has become academic information.” — Shri Abhijan Das, Strategic Consultant “Space has become one of the most essential components of a nation's defence and security architecture. If we look at modern conflicts around the world, it is clear that space-based capabilities are no longer optional—they are increasingly central to how security and warfare are understood.” — Dr. PRAMOD KUMAR KONUGURTHI, Senior Vice President, XDLINX Space Labs “Building indigenous space assets is not only about meeting an immediate requirement. story-4c2ebe0987de46201d06c497.content: 🔴 هام جداً .. عملية "في قلب العدو" .. كيف وماذا استهدفت الضربة داخل صنعاء؟ كشفت وكالة "شيبا للاستخبارات" عن عملية أمنية وعسكرية قالت إنها نُفذت فجر الجمعة الماضية في عمق صنعاء، واستهدفت شبكة اتصالات سرية مرتبطة بمنظومة القيادة والسيطرة الحوثية، بهدف إحباط هجوم كبير كان الحرس الثوري الإيراني يخطط لتنفيذه ضد السعودية من الأراضي اليمنية. العملية حملت اسم "في قلب العدو"، وجمعت بين تحرك جوي وآخر بري؛ إذ استخدمت طائرات مسيرة لتحديد وتتبع عقد شبكة اتصالات تعمل عبر الألياف الضوئية، بالتزامن مع استهداف فريق أرضي لغرفة اتصالات رئيسية داخل صنعاء. 📌 وبحسب المصادر، قتل في الضربة أربعة خبراء إيرانيين مرتبطين بالشبكة، فيما كان داخل الموقع عدد من الشخصيات الحوثية البارزة، دون أن تتمكن الوكالة من تأكيد مقتل أي قيادي حوثي. وتكمن أهمية الشبكة، وفقا للتقرير، في ارتباطها بالبنية العسكرية ومنظومة القيادة والتنسيق الحوثية، مع الإشارة إلى ارتباط اسم محمد حسين بدر الدين الحوثي، شقيق عبد الملك الحوثي، بالإشراف على ملف الاتصالات العسكرية، إلى جانب جهاز داخلي يعرف باسم "الاتصالات الجهادية" ويتولى الاتصالات الحساسة. 🔴 لماذا استُهدفت الشبكة؟ تربط @shebaintelligen العملية بتحركات إيرانية قالت إن الحرس الثوري شارك مباشرة في التخطيط والإعداد لهجوم كبير ضد السعودية. لم يكن استهداف الاتصالات هدفا منفصلا، بل محاولة لتعطيل منظومة القيادة والتنسيق المستخدمة في الإعداد للهجوم، فيما تحفظت الوكالة عن كشف أهداف الهجوم المفترض داخل السعودية أو نوعية القدرات التي كانت ستستخدم فيه. وبالتزامن، ظهرت مسيرات SKYWASP "دبور السماء" عملياتيا في أجواء صنعاء للمرة الأولى .. حيث نفذت ضربات حول العاصمة استهدفت مواقع للدفاعات الجوية ومخازن أسلحة ومنشآت مرتبطة بالصواريخ والطائرات المسيرة، خصوصا في محيط جبلي عيبان ونقم. 📌 الاستهداف لم يقتصر على صنعاء. التقرير تحدث عن هجمات طالت منشآت اتصالات في تعز، بينها مواقع في الذكرة والحوبان والراهدة، بالتزامن مع تقارير عن هجوم إلكتروني استهدف شبكات اتصالات خاضعة للحوثيين وأدى إلى اضطرابات في خدمات الاتصالات والإنترنت. وبذلك، ترسم المعلومات التي أوردتها شيبا صورة لعملية متعددة المسارات، جمعت بين الضربات الجوية والعمل البري والهجمات الإلكترونية، بهدف الضغط على شبكة الاتصالات ومنظومة القيادة والسيطرة الحوثية، في وقت تتحدث فيه الوكالة عن استعدادات لهجوم إيراني محتمل ضد السعودية.

story-5145d4140213e017bf7805c5.content: 🚨🇺🇸🇨🇳 A chatbot hallucination nearly had American troops boarding a Chinese ship in the middle of the Iran war An analyst at Special Operations Command asked an AI about a ship's manifest, the bot blended open-source material with classified signals intelligence and decided the vessel was carrying NUCLEAR WEAPON components, and then the same analyst used AI again to write it up as a formal intelligence report that went out across the military. Planes were in the air and armed personnel were preparing to board before somebody finally checked how the report was built and found the whole thing was, in one source's words, entirely false. Another source put it more bluntly, saying it almost started a war, which is not an exaggeration when the target is a Chinese ship. Hegseth's AI strategy in January promised to eliminate bureaucratic barriers and put these models in the hands of three million personnel at every classification level, and this is what that looks like when nobody has agreed on how to verify the output. One official's summary deserves a plaque somewhere in the Pentagon: AI allows you to get to a bad idea faster. Targeting is the next frontier for these tools, with no rules yet for how a human in the loop prevents killing the wrong people, so the question isn't whether this happens again but whether the next one gets caught BEFORE the boarding party leaves... Source: CNN / Writer: Daniel, Lucas

story-5302f33e28c6e8ce4256d474.content: 🚨 PEOPLE BUILDING AT THE TOP AI LABS ARE WARNING THAT AI COULD DESTROY HUMANITY WITHIN THE NEXT 10 YEARS Jacob Coxon, who spent 3 years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic, resigned from Anthropic today. His words: "Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives." He says the people actually building this technology privately believe it could kill everyone by the end of the decade, they just don't say that publicly. He says OpenAI staff haven't fully grasped what's at stake, while Anthropic staff understand it clearly but keep racing anyway, because they believe if they don't build it first, someone less careful will. He's not the first safety researcher to say something like this. In February 2026, Anthropic's own head of safety, Mrinank Sharma, resigned saying "the world is in peril," citing the same tension Coxon describes: safety commitments losing out to competitive pressure. Back in 2024, OpenAI's two most senior safety leaders, Jan Leike and Ilya Sutskever, both quit within days of each other. Leike said "safety culture and processes have taken a backseat to shiny products," meaning OpenAI kept shipping flashy new features and models faster than its safety team could properly vet them, prioritizing speed and PR wins over caution. This same pattern shows up outside the AI companies too, in how they've handled outside pressure. Earlier this year, a Google DeepMind researcher named Alex Turner spent months trying to stop Google from signing an unrestricted military AI contract with the Pentagon. He organized an internal petition signed by 250 employees, personally lobbied top AI scientists like Yoshua Bengio and Stuart Russell to speak out publicly, and even messaged Google's CEO directly. Almost no one acted. Google signed the deal anyway, with no binding restrictions on weapons use. Turner resigned soon after. Google's Chief Scientist, Jeff Dean, had personally signed a 2018 pledge promising to never support lethal autonomous weapons. He stayed through the Pentagon deal. In August 2026, he left Google entirely. Another former DeepMind researcher, Jonathan Richard Schwarz, added his own warning after 7 years at the lab: "I left DeepMind after 7 years, and since rejected offers to join the other two, due to severe concerns about the concentration of power these labs represent. What is currently happening in this field is deeply unhealthy for society." In every case, staff raised safety concerns internally, got overruled by competitive or commercial pressure, and left once the decision was made.

story-5516bd991836a93b1923fb25.content: Much of the debate over superpowers, AGI, and the geopolitical balance of power is simply a replay of the debate that got underway about 15 years ago regarding international efforts to limit L.A.W.S. (lethal autonomous weapons systems) and “killer robots.” That debate featured almost all the same type of proposals we hear discussed today for AGI: global accords / treaties, non-proliferation agreements, R&D controls, surveillance efforts, and even potential unilateral or bilateral covert or kinetic action. Some control advocates had no qualms about floating that final option even though they were suggesting we should be willing to substitute one type of very real existential risk (global armed conflict / thermonuclear war) for a different theoretical existential risk (all the various “Terminator”-esque robot takeover scenarios). Anyway, there was a lot of academic and political activity surrounding all of this that culminated in the “Campaign to Stop Killer Robots,” the “Lethal Autonomous Weapons Pledge,” and a host of other arms control proposals. [FYI, I summarized those efforts in a 2023 white paper on “Existential Risks and Global Governance Issues around AI and Robotics”: https://t.co/NONpxXIDY8] Those “killer robot” control efforts quietly faded away to some extent.** Yet, all the same ideas are back on the table for AGI / “superintelligence.” The past is prologue, as they say. Nonetheless, it is strange how so few people talk about this very recent history when discussing responses to AGI development by superpowers or other nations. --- ** The drone war in Ukraine has opened up a new debate (and corresponding body of academic literature and policy writing) over how “killer robots” can change the nature of modern warfare and balance the odds in favor of an underdog looking to defend itself against a larger aggressor. It is interesting to me how the “Campaign to Stop Killer Robots” and Lethal Autonomous Weapons Pledge efforts seemed to fizzle somewhat as the Russia-Ukraine conflict got underway. Just a random observation. I am writing about this currently in a new paper.

story-5d45213a94c46f51c9091085.content: 🇷🇺 RUSSIA | Alabuga is becoming a heavily protected drone-production complex I analysed the latest satellite imagery of the Alabuga complex in Tatarstan, one of Russia’s key production centres for long-range Shahed/Geran-family drones. The imagery shows that the site is still expanding, while defensive infrastructure around the main production area is becoming increasingly extensive. PRODUCTION SCALE Russia initially relied on Iranian-designed Shahed drones before establishing large-scale domestic production at Alabuga. According to CSIS, production capacity at the complex had exceeded 5,500 drones per month by early 2026. Ukrainian intelligence later estimated that Russia was also producing around 3,000 jet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones per month. CONTINUING EXPANSION By comparing satellite imagery from different periods, I can clearly see how the industrial footprint of the complex has expanded. Some infrastructure existed before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, but additional production halls, warehouses, logistics facilities, residential buildings and supporting infrastructure have appeared during the following years. The scale of construction increased particularly strongly during 2025 and continued into 2026. NEW PROTECTIVE STRUCTURES The latest imagery shows dozens of tall lattice structures positioned around key production facilities. I can identify two separate defensive perimeters surrounding the main industrial area. These structures appear designed to support large protective nets or mesh barriers intended to complicate attacks by long-range drones or cruise missiles. The defensive system is unusual in scale and demonstrates how important the Alabuga complex has become to Russia’s long-range strike capability. AIR DEFENCE Open-source analysis published in 2026 identified at least 23 air-defence positions around the Alabuga area, including sites associated with systems such as Pantsir-S1 and Tor. Additional defensive positions and protective infrastructure continue to appear around the complex. Alabuga was first confirmed struck by Ukrainian long-range drones on 2 April 2024. Since then, both the production facilities and the defensive network surrounding the site have expanded significantly. The satellite record shows how Alabuga has evolved from an industrial production site into one of the most heavily protected elements of Russia’s drone-production infrastructure. #MizarVision #SatelliteImagery #Alabuga #OSINT
